children: NSE IPO anchor book saw LIC emerge as the largest investor with a Rs 465 crore allocation ahead of the Rs 22,561 crore public issue

Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) emerged as the largest investor in the anchor book of the National Stock Exchange of India’s (NSE) Rs 22,561.57 crore initial public offering (IPO), committing about Rs 465 crore ahead of the public issue. The exchange raised Rs 6,746.18 crore from 189 anchor investors at the upper end of the price band of Rs 1,785 per share.

LIC, which already holds a 10.72 per cent stake in NSE, received around Rs 465.3 crore worth of shares in the anchor allocation. The participation came as NSE prepared for one of India’s largest IPOs, with the issue comprising an offer for sale by existing shareholders.

The anchor book also attracted major global and domestic institutional investors, including Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global, the Monetary Authority of Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Fidelity, Goldman Sachs and several domestic mutual funds.
Domestic mutual funds received 36.98 per cent of the total anchor allocation, with 29 mutual funds applying through 98 schemes.
Life insurance companies and pension funds accounted for another 16.04 per cent of the allocation. The NSE IPO had a price band of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share and comprised up to 12.64 crore shares.
Since the issue was entirely an OFS, NSE itself would not receive proceeds from the IPO, with the money accruing to the selling shareholders after expenses.

The IPO subsequently received strong demand from institutional investors. By the second day of bidding, the issue was fully subscribed, with qualified institutional buyers and non-institutional investors driving demand. The issue eventually closed with 5.71 times subscription, receiving bids for 50.58 crore shares against 8.86 crore shares on offer.

The QIB portion was subscribed 12.68 times, while the NII category received 6.55 times subscription and the retail portion 1.39 times. NSE shares are scheduled to list on the BSE on 24 September. The IPO marks the exchange’s long-awaited public-market debut after years of regulatory and legal hurdles delayed the listing process.
